prs.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
prs.author: adityuhkapoor
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same root cause in pre_parse_json: the pre-existing check `field_info.annotation is not str` triggers JSON-parsing on any non-plain-`str` annotation, including unions like `str | None`, `str | int`, etc. This means a plain string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. "null", "123", "[1,2]") gets incorrectly decoded instead of passed through as a string, corrupting valid input for any union-with-str parameter. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same root cause in pre_parse_json: the pre-existing check `field_info.annotation is not str` triggers JSON-parsing on any non-plain-`str` annotation, including unions like `str | None`, `str | int`, etc. This means a plain string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. "null", "123", "[1,2]") gets incorrectly decoded instead of passed through as a string, corrupting valid input for any union-with-str parameter. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json`/`_SIMPLE_TYPES` generalizes the fix to any union composed entirely of JSON-primitive types (str, int, float, bool, None), which is a superset of the fix in #3056's `_is_optional_str`, which only special-cases the `str | None` (Optional[str]) case specifically. Since a `str | None` union is itself a union of two members from `_SIMPLE_TYPES`, #2032's check already returns False (skip parsing) for exactly the case #3056 targets, so #3056's fix is fully subsumed. Both PRs add tests to the same block of tests/server/mcpserver/test_func_metadata.py, so merging both would produce a direct conflict.

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 detects the collision with a plain `if request_id in self._request_streams` check using `str(message.id)` as the key, which still collapses the JSON-RPC int id `1` and the string id "1" into the same key string — so it can falsely 409 a distinct id, and it doesn't address that a string id equal to the literal "_GET_stream" would collide with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY sentinel. #3221 introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:` before the id) that fixes the duplicate-id race for the general case *and* both of these adjacent edge cases in the same code path, so it's the more complete fix for the identical root cause rather than a narrower version of it.

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 implements __reduce__ once on the base MCPError class using MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ restore, so it fixes pickling for every current and future MCPError subclass without per-type branching. 2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, leaving other subclasses (e.g. NoBackChannelError) unfixed. 2478's _restore_mcp_error hardcodes an 'if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError' special case and relies on from_error/from_error_data classmethods, which requires updating the dispatch function whenever a new subclass with an incompatible constructor is added. 3262's test file additionally imports and exercises NoBackChannelError for pickle round-tripping, demonstrating the broader coverage its base-class fix provides, and it's branched from a later revision of exceptions.py (index c2a7fd44e7 vs f153ea319d for the other two), so it reflects the more current state of the file.

clusters.pick_reason: #2858 is a rebase of a stale, previously-unmerged PR (#2660); its visible diff only shows leftover import cleanup, with the actual lock-scope change not evident in the current diff. #3252 narrows the window by moving `response = yield request` outside `async with self.context.lock`, cutting contention, but still uses a plain anyio.Lock, which requires acquire/release on the same task — a hazard if httpx resumes or closes the auth-flow generator from a different task. #3243 performs the same yield-outside-lock change and additionally replaces the lock with a task-agnostic anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1), and splits out a separate flow_lock so refresh/authorization transitions stay single-flight while unrelated resource requests are never serialized behind them — a superset of #3252's fix that also removes the task-reentrancy hazard.

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 implements __reduce__ once on the base MCPError class using MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ restore, so it fixes pickling for every current and future MCPError subclass without per-type branching. 2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, leaving other subclasses (e.g. NoBackChannelError) unfixed. 2478's _restore_mcp_error hardcodes an 'if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError' special case and relies on from_error/from_error_data classmethods, which requires updating the dispatch function whenever a new subclass with an incompatible constructor is added. 3262's test file additionally imports and exercises NoBackChannelError for pickle round-tripping, demonstrating the broader coverage its base-class fix provides, and it's branched from a later revision of exceptions.py (index c2a7fd44e7 vs f153ea319d for the other two), so it reflects the more current state of the file.

clusters.pick_reason: #2858 is a rebase of a stale, previously-unmerged PR (#2660); its visible diff only shows leftover import cleanup, with the actual lock-scope change not evident in the current diff. #3252 narrows the window by moving `response = yield request` outside `async with self.context.lock`, cutting contention, but still uses a plain anyio.Lock, which requires acquire/release on the same task — a hazard if httpx resumes or closes the auth-flow generator from a different task. #3243 performs the same yield-outside-lock change and additionally replaces the lock with a task-agnostic anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1), and splits out a separate flow_lock so refresh/authorization transitions stay single-flight while unrelated resource requests are never serialized behind them — a superset of #3252's fix that also removes the task-reentrancy hazard.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 detects the collision with a plain `if request_id in self._request_streams` check using `str(message.id)` as the key, which still collapses the JSON-RPC int id `1` and the string id "1" into the same key string — so it can falsely 409 a distinct id, and it doesn't address that a string id equal to the literal "_GET_stream" would collide with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY sentinel. #3221 introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:` before the id) that fixes the duplicate-id race for the general case *and* both of these adjacent edge cases in the same code path, so it's the more complete fix for the identical root cause rather than a narrower version of it.
